sources.title: US imposes sanctions on dozens linked to Iran's shadow banking networks
Brazil's Raizen capitalization plan to close near top of target range, sources say
Brazil cuts 2027 GDP forecast, raises inflation outlook but remains more upbeat than market

stories.topic: SINGAPORE / HONG KONG / UAE / US TREASURY / FINCEN / IRAN / BANKING / SANCTIONS
stories.headline: US sanctions add a concrete development to retained Iran-compliance warnings
stories.body: Reuters reported new US sanctions on dozens of people and entities linked to alleged Iranian shadow banking. FinCEN identified nearly US$15bn of potentially related global financial activity from January 2025 through August 2026, including connections through businesses in Singapore, Hong Kong and the UAE across oil, shipping and investment. That figure is global potential activity, not a Singapore-only total or a finding against a particular Singapore bank. No attributable SGD or bank-share reaction was established.
stories.analysis: New designations require counterparty review; allegations and network connections do not establish wrongdoing by unrelated institutions.
stories.watch_next: Formal designation identifiers and regulatory guidance.
stories.earlier: Retained v1 at the 20 November 23:37:27 SGT cutoff covered US Treasury compliance warnings to Singapore and Malaysia. This v2 adds sanctions and the dated FinCEN analysis, rather than repeating those warnings.

stories.topic: BRAZIL / RAIZEN / SHELL / COSAN / CORPORATE CREDIT / RESTRUCTURING
stories.headline: Sources expect Raizen capital raising near its upper target; proceeds remain unconfirmed
stories.body: Reuters sources expected the capital raising in Brazil’s Raizen debt restructuring to finish near its upper BRL39.8bn target, which includes a BRL3.5bn commitment from investor Shell plc. Co-founder Rubens Ometto might withhold additional investment, potentially diluting his ownership. The report describes expected funding and commitments, not confirmed receipt of the full target or a completed restructuring. No attributable bond-price or credit-spread movement was established.
stories.analysis: Final funding and debt terms determine liquidity and potential recoveries; a target is not an assured outcome.
stories.watch_next: Subscription results, cash actually received and post-restructuring debt.

stories.topic: BRAZIL / GDP / INFLATION / BRL / ECONOMIC FORECASTS / SOVEREIGN CREDIT
stories.headline: Brazil lowers its 2027 growth forecast to 1.8% and lifts inflation forecast to 4.5%
stories.body: Reuters reported Brazil’s Finance Ministry cutting its 2027 gross domestic product growth forecast from 2.3% to 1.8% and raising its inflation projection from 3.8% to 4.5%. Private economists in the central-bank survey expected 1.0% growth and 5.1% inflation for 2027. Borrowing costs and weaker growth drivers shaped the revision. These are forecasts for the same year, not realised growth or CPI. Reuters’s nearly 20% real depreciation refers to performance against USD since the previous month’s election, not a reaction isolated to this announcement.
stories.analysis: Weaker forecast growth alongside higher forecast inflation can complicate debt service and policy choices.
stories.watch_next: Budget revisions, central-bank guidance and financing conditions.
